questions.question: For an n-bit function, how many classical queries are needed in the worst case to determine if it's constant or balanced?
questions.explanation: In the worst case, a classical algorithm must query more than half the inputs. After 2^(n-1) queries all returning the same value, you still can't be sure — you need one more query to confirm.

questions.question: What measurement outcome indicates the function is constant?
options: All zeros on the input qubits
All ones on the input qubits
questions.explanation: If f is constant, the final Hadamard concentrates all amplitude on |0...0⟩. Measuring all zeros means f is constant.

questions.question: What is the role of the ancilla qubit prepared in |−⟩?
options: It stores the output of f
It enables phase kickback — encoding f(x) as a phase on input qubits
It entangles with the input qubits
questions.explanation: The ancilla in |−⟩ enables phase kickback: Uf|x⟩|−⟩ = (-1)^f(x)|x⟩|−⟩. The function value becomes a phase factor on the input register.
